props.html:
Direct answer

Sydney Paintmasters is a licensed painting contractor covering all 20 Inner West suburbs, from Balmain and Rozelle through Newtown and Marrickville to Tempe and Sydenham. We hold Painter Decorator Licence 315254C, we have been painting for more than 20 years, and we quote fixed prices with no call-out fee. Interior, exterior, heritage, strata, commercial, roof, epoxy and pool work, six days a week.

What does it cost?

Every Inner West quote is fixed price and free. The number depends on surface area, prep, access and coat count. No call-out fee to find out.

Are you licensed?

Yes. Painter Decorator Licence 315254C, searchable on the NSW Fair Trading register. Public liability cover is current.

Do you do heritage?

Yes. Much of the Inner West sits inside a heritage conservation area. We work to streetscape-sympathetic schemes and Council controls.

How fast can you start?

Call 0423 019 087 during business hours and we will book a site visit.

props.label: Services
props.html:
What we paint

Painting services across the Inner West

Nine services, one crew, one licence number. Residential through to commercial, and everything the local building stock throws at us. Terraces with no side path. Federation cottages with fretwork. Walk-up flats with tired common areas. Cafes that cannot close.

House Painting Inner West

Full-home repaints on terraces, cottages, semis and townhouses. Washing, filling, sanding and priming before a single topcoat goes on. That prep stage is where a paint job in the Inner West is won or lost.

Interior Painting Inner West

Walls, ceilings, cornices, skirtings, architraves and doors. Low-odour and low-VOC options for occupied Inner West homes, so you can stay put while we work room by room.

Exterior Painting Inner West

Rendered facades, face brick, weatherboard, timber trims, balconies and fences. Sydney UV, humidity and traffic grime chew through cheap coatings. We spec systems that survive an Inner West street.

Strata Painting Inner West

Common areas, stairwells, foyers, balconies, car parks and facades. Ashfield and Marrickville carry serious walk-up flat stock. We scope the job clearly enough that a strata committee can sign it off without a second meeting.

Commercial Painting Inner West

Shopfronts, cafes, studios, warehouses and retail fitouts. King Street, Norton Street, Darling Street and Marrickville Road do not stop trading for us, so we work around opening hours.

Office Painting Inner West

Fitouts, meeting rooms, corridors and reception areas. After-hours and weekend scheduling available so nobody in your Inner West office loses a working day to drop sheets.

Roof Painting Inner West

Tile and metal roof cleaning, repairs and two-coat coating. A tired roof drags down the whole facade. Height access and edge protection are quoted upfront, never added later.

Epoxy Flooring Inner West

Garages, warehouse floors, workshops and basement car parks. Hard-wearing, easy to clean, and a genuinely different finish from a rolled-on garage paint. Marrickville and Sydenham warehouse conversions are our regular ground here.

Pool Painting Inner West

Concrete pool preparation, etching and coating. Not a service most Inner West painters offer, and doing it properly means treating the shell before anything gets applied to it.

props.html:
Where we work

Inner West suburbs, covered properly

Twenty suburbs, and they are not interchangeable. A Balmain sandstone cottage and a Sydenham warehouse have almost nothing in common except a postcode range. Four suburbs get their own full page. The rest are set out below.

Also covers Balmain East and Birchgrove.Painter NewtownKing Street shopfronts and wall-to-wall Victorian terrace rows with no side access.Painter MarrickvilleWorkers cottages, brick terraces, post-war fibro and the converted warehouse sector.Painter LeichhardtNorton Street and the terrace belt, covering Annandale, Rozelle and Lilyfield.
Ashfield NSW 2131

Painters in Ashfield

Ashfield has the widest housing mix in the Inner West. Grand Victorian mansions on Victoria Street sit a few blocks from Federation Queen Anne cottages, and both are surrounded by interwar and post-war walk-up flats. Three very different painting jobs in one postcode.

The flats are where most of the work is. Common areas, stairwells, balcony soffits and rendered facades on blocks that have not been touched in a decade. We scope strata jobs so the committee can see exactly what is being painted and what is not, which is usually the thing that stalls a vote.

One thing worth knowing about Ashfield. Its heritage protection is estate-level, not suburb-wide. The Harland Estate, Miller Avenue, Murrell Estate and Service Avenue conservation areas each cover a handful of streets. So colour and materials rules can apply to your street and not your neighbour's. We check the map before we quote a scheme, rather than after.

Federation face brick, ornate plaster, palm-lined streets. Ashfield rewards careful prep. Compare with Haberfield, where the rules apply to every single house.

Call 0423 019 087 for a fixed-price Ashfield quote.

Haberfield NSW 2045

Painters in Haberfield: Australia's first garden suburb

Haberfield is the one Inner West suburb where the heritage conservation area covers essentially the whole thing. Council designates it C54, and it has its own dedicated chapter in the Inner West Development Control Plan, Chapter E2, Haberfield Neighbourhood. That is unusual. Most suburbs get a paragraph.

What that means for a repaint is straightforward. The suburb is Australia's first planned garden suburb, laid out at the turn of the twentieth century with single-storey brick houses on generous garden lots, consistent setbacks and a shared palette of forms and materials. Exterior colour schemes are expected to be sympathetic to that streetscape. Timber fretwork, tiled front verandahs, roughcast gable ends and original joinery all need to be treated as fabric worth keeping, not as surfaces to be flattened under two coats of whatever is on special.

We do not need to overstate this. Minor works like repainting generally do not require a Development Application. But the colour you choose and the way the original detail is prepared do matter here, both to Council and to the resale value of the house. If you want certainty, Inner West Council can confirm what applies to your property.

Federation Queen Anne, done right. Request a Haberfield colour and prep scope.

Dulwich Hill NSW 2203

Painters in Dulwich Hill

Dulwich Hill is one of the biggest suburbs in the Inner West by population, and it has quietly become one of the busiest renovation markets. Federation and interwar cottages, partial conservation area coverage across several pockets, and a steady flow of owner-occupiers finally getting to the exterior after doing the kitchen.

Light rail brought a lot of that. New owners, older houses, tired weatherboard and render. Our usual Dulwich Hill job is a full exterior with timber repairs built into the scope rather than discovered halfway through.

See our Marrickville painting page, our nearest full service page.

Summer Hill 2130 · Lewisham 2049 · Petersham 2049

Painters in Summer Hill, Lewisham and Petersham

The rail corridor village belt. Summer Hill leads it, with a compact high street around the station and a lot of Federation and Victorian cottage stock that is being brought back to life street by street. Demand for painters here has climbed steadily over the past year, which tracks with what we see on the ground.

Petersham brings the conservation area terraces and the Portuguese strip along New Canterbury Road, where shopfront repaints need to happen without shutting a business for a week. Lewisham is quieter, sitting between the two along the Old Canterbury Road corridor, with the same Victorian and Federation cottages and partial heritage coverage.

Same building stock, three different streetscapes. Our Newtown page covers the terrace work in detail.

Stanmore 2048 · Enmore 2042

Painters in Stanmore and Enmore

Stanmore is grand Victorian terraces and villas on unusually wide streets, inside a conservation area, with a strip of Parramatta Road frontage stock at the northern edge. Enmore is Enmore Road: shopfronts, the theatre, and rows of Victorian speculative terraces running off it.

Both sit inside the same heritage conservation area that governs Newtown, so the colour and detail rules are the same ones. We have set that out properly on the Newtown painting page, rather than repeat it here.

St Peters 2044 · Sydenham 2044 · Tempe 2044

Painters in St Peters, Sydenham and Tempe

The southern corridor, and the most commercial-leaning part of our Inner West work. Tempe carries the most residential demand of the three: post-war and interwar cottages near the Cooks River, plus houses on high-traffic corridors where exterior surfaces take a beating from grime and need a harder-wearing system than a quiet back street would.

Sydenham is warehouse and light industrial territory. Factory walls, roller doors, epoxy floors and the small residential pocket that survived the flight path. St Peters brings Victorian workers cottages and the brickworks heritage a/nsw/painter-inner-westround Sydney Park, with WestConnex corridor dust as an ongoing maintenance factor for anything facing the road.

Warehouses, cottages, roller doors. The Marrickville page covers our warehouse conversion work.

props.label: Process
props.html:
How it runs

Three steps, no surprises

Most painting complaints trace back to a vague quote. So we do not give vague quotes.

01

Site visit and fixed quote

We come to your Inner West property, measure it, look at the substrate, check the access, and write a fixed price against a defined scope. Free, and no call-out fee. You will see what is included, coat by coat, and what is not.

02

Prep, protect, paint

Furniture and floors covered before anything else happens. Then washing, scraping, filling, sanding and priming. Only then does colour go on. We work around your household, your tenants or your trading hours, and we clean up at the end of every day rather than the end of the job.

03

Walkthrough and sign-off

We walk the job with you before we pack up. Anything you are not happy with gets fixed then and there, not scheduled for a return visit that never comes.

props.label: Three things the Inner West actually needs
props.html:
Where we are different

Three things the Inner West actually needs

Not a list of adjectives. These are the three problems we get called about most, and they are specific to how this part of Sydney is built.

Character properties without the damage

Terraces, cottages, apartments, townhouses, shopfronts and renovated homes all sit side by side here. Older surfaces need patience: careful preparation, clean cut-in lines, low-odour paint options, and finishes chosen to suit period detail rather than bury it. We are just as comfortable on a crisp modern interior. The point is knowing which one you are standing in.

Exteriors in tight Inner West streets

Narrow side paths. Shared boundary walls. Neighbouring properties a metre away. Balconies you cannot reach from the ground. Getting an exterior repaint done here is as much a planning and access problem as a painting one. We organise scaffold, drop zones and neighbour access before the job starts, and we leave the street the way we found it.

Low-disruption work for busy places

Rentals between tenants. Strata buildings full of residents. Cafes, offices, studios and retail spaces that cannot afford to close. We schedule around you, keep work zones clean and contained, use durable finishes on high-traffic surfaces, and hand back fast. Nobody wants a painter for three weeks longer than they need one.

props.label: Faq
props.html:
Booking, quoting and insurance

Common questions before you book

The seven things people ask us on the first phone call.

How much does a painter cost in the Inner West?
There is no honest flat rate. The price of an Inner West repaint depends on the surface area, the condition of the substrate, how much preparation and repair is needed, how hard the property is to access, and how many coats the system calls for. A tidy interior refresh and a full heritage exterior with render repairs are not in the same league. We give you a fixed price after we have looked at the actual property, not a guess from photos. The site visit is free and there is no call-out fee. Call 0423 019 087.
How do I book a painter in the Inner West?
Call 0423 019 087 or send the quote form on this page. We will arrange a site visit at your property, walk the job with you, and write a fixed-price quote against a defined scope. Once you accept the quote we lock in dates. We are on the tools 6am to 6pm Monday to Saturday and closed Sunday.
Is the quote free, and is there a call-out fee?
The quote is free and there is no call-out fee. You pay nothing to have us come out, look at the property, and give you a written fixed price. If the number does not suit you, that is the end of it.
Are you licensed and insured?
Yes. Sydney Paintmasters holds Painter Decorator Licence 315254C, which you can check yourself on the NSW Fair Trading contractor licence register. We carry current public liability insurance. Always ask any painter for their licence number before they start, and check it.
How long does an Inner West house repaint take?
It depends on the size and the prep. A single-room refresh can be a day. A full interior repaint of a terrace usually runs across several days. A full exterior with render repairs, heritage detail and scaffold access takes longer again, because the preparation stage is where most of the time goes. We put an indicative duration on the written quote so you can plan around it.
Do you charge a fixed price or an hourly rate?
Fixed price, every time. You get one number against one written scope, so you know exactly what is being painted and what is not before anyone picks up a brush. Hourly rates on a painting job put all the risk on the customer, and we do not think that is fair.
Can we stay in the house while you paint?
Yes, most of our Inner West clients do. We work room by room, keep the work zone contained, cover floors and furniture, and pack up the site at the end of each day. Ask us for low-odour and low-VOC products and we will spec them into the quote, which makes staying put a lot more comfortable, particularly with small children or anyone working from home.

props.label: Local Faq
props.html:
Local questions

Painting an Inner West property: what is different

Heritage rules, terrace access, strata and shopfronts. The seven local questions.

Do you paint heritage conservation area homes in the Inner West?
Yes, and it is a large part of what we do here. The Inner West holds one of the densest concentrations of heritage conservation areas in Sydney. Haberfield is covered almost entirely by one. Balmain, Annandale, Newtown, Enmore, Stanmore, Petersham and Rozelle all carry substantial coverage, and Ashfield, Dulwich Hill, Lewisham, Summer Hill and St Peters carry it across parts of their streets. We work to streetscape-sympathetic colour schemes and treat original detail as fabric to preserve.
Do I need council approval to repaint a heritage home in the Inner West?
Generally, no. Minor works such as repainting an existing painted surface usually do not require a Development Application. But conservation area controls do shape what is appropriate, particularly for exterior colour schemes and for original unpainted surfaces such as face brick or sandstone, which are often better left alone. Inner West Council is the only party who can give you a definitive answer for your specific property, and we will point you to them rather than guess on your behalf.
Which Inner West suburbs do you cover?
All 20 official Inner West suburbs: Annandale, Ashfield, Balmain, Balmain East, Birchgrove, Dulwich Hill, Enmore, Haberfield, Leichhardt, Lewisham, Lilyfield, Marrickville, Newtown, Petersham, Rozelle, Stanmore, St Peters, Summer Hill, Sydenham and Tempe. Call 0423 019 087 and tell us the suburb.
Do you do strata painting for Inner West apartment blocks?
Yes. Common areas, stairwells, foyers, balcony soffits, car parks and full facades. Ashfield and Marrickville in particular carry a lot of interwar and post-war walk-up flat stock that is due for a repaint. We write strata scopes in plain language with the inclusions and exclusions set out clearly, because a vague scope is what sends a committee back for a second meeting.
Can you paint a terrace with no side access?
Yes. It is the normal condition in Newtown, Enmore, Stanmore, Balmain and Annandale, where terraces share boundary walls on both sides and have no side path at all. The front facade is worked from the street, and the rear and upper levels are reached by scaffold or a swing stage. We plan the access, the drop zones and any neighbour permissions before the job starts, and we price all of it into the fixed quote rather than adding it later.
Do you paint shopfronts and cafes in the Inner West?
Yes. King Street, Enmore Road, Norton Street, Darling Street, Marrickville Road and New Canterbury Road are all regular ground for us. Retail and hospitality cannot afford to close, so we schedule after-hours and weekend work and hand the space back trading-ready. Ask about low-odour systems if you have a food business.
What paint holds up best in Inner West conditions?
Inner West exteriors cop strong UV, high humidity, driving rain and, on the busy corridors, a constant film of traffic grime. Peninsula properties near Iron Cove and the harbour add salt exposure to that list. The right system depends on the substrate: render, face brick, weatherboard and rendered masonry all want different primers. What matters more than the brand on the tin is the preparation underneath it. We specify the full system, primer through topcoat, on the written quote.
